svg.title: Faded maritime book paragraphs
svg.desc: Original decorative prose, typeset in Old Standard TT. Letter outlines keep the book typography consistent without loading a webfont.
svg.metadata:
Far beyond the last familiar headland, the sea opened into a country without roads or boundaries. The ship carried her small company through its changing light, while the wind turned each sail towards a horizon that seemed always to withdraw. Behind them lay the harbour, already more memory than place.
At dawn the watch found the water silver beneath a pale and cloudless sky. A gull crossed the wake and vanished. Nothing disturbed the broad circle of the ocean except the measured rise of the bow, the creaking of the timbers, and the long white road that followed in their course.
The old charts were spread upon the cabin table, their corners held against the motion of the vessel. Names of distant islands lay beside empty spaces where no soundings had been marked. Across those spaces a patient hand had traced the passage of a whale, and with it the course of an uncertain voyage.
There were hours when every man aboard seemed to listen for some word the ocean would not speak. The captain stood apart beneath the weathered rigging, his face turned towards the light. Around him the ship went about her ancient business, rope by rope and watch by watch, as ships had done for generations.
Beneath the surface lay another world, quiet and immense. The daylight thinned through green water into blue, and the blue gave way to darkness. Through that depth the great whale travelled with an ease no vessel could possess, his pale back passing like a cloud beneath the scattered brightness of the waves.
By evening the wind had freshened. Shadows gathered in the folds of the canvas and the sea began to show its darker colour. A lantern was brought below, a course entered in the log, and the men who had finished their watch went slowly towards the warmth and close air of the forecastle.
Still the ship pressed onward. Each mile carried her farther from the common world of doors and streets, of gardens, bells, and voices calling from the shore. Here there was only the weather, the deep water, and the purpose that had brought them all together beneath those narrow strips of sail.
The next morning promised neither favour nor warning. Light returned across the water, touching the mastheads before it reached the deck. Far out upon the swell a brief white gleam appeared and was gone. The lookout leaned forward, shading his eyes, while below him the vessel continued on her course.
And so the distance narrowed between hunter and quarry. Above, the rigging hummed in the rising wind; below, the unseen currents moved through their older paths. The ocean held them both within its great circumference, and the last page of the voyage waited, as yet unwritten, beyond the next line of waves.
